title: Set a lead brick between each hot vial and the technologist's seat
instruction: The two yellow vials are radioactive and must not be touched or moved: stand one grey lead brick upright on the table across the straight line from each vial to the blue block, where the technologist sits, within 12 cm of that vial. The left arm can pass the second brick to the right arm on the green pad.
context: On a hot-lab bench, staff put temporary lead shielding between radioactive sources and where people sit, close to the source, where a small shield blocks the most; no spot is marked, it follows from where the source and the person are. This is a reduced version with one brick per vial. Unlike line-of-sight hiding tasks, the robot places a blocker on the line from a hazard to a person, close to the hazard, without touching the hazard. Done by: nuclear medicine technologists, radiopharmacists.
setup: Two yellow plastic vials (cylinders 3 cm across, 5 cm tall, 50 g each) stand upright, their centres 25 cm in front of the arm bases, one 15 cm left of centre and one 15 cm right of centre; they are loose and must not be handled. A blue painted wooden block, 15 cm front to back, 20 cm side to side and 12 cm tall, is fixed on the centre line, its centre 70 cm in front of the arm bases; it marks the technologist's seat and is out of the arms' reach. An open orange plastic rack is fixed in front of the left arm, its centre 25 cm in front of the arm bases and 36 cm left of centre: a 1 cm floor inside four 1 cm walls, 3 cm tall from the table, inside 17 cm front to back and 14 cm side to side. Two dark grey painted wooden (or dense plastic) boxes, stand-ins for lead bricks (5 cm front to back, 12 cm side to side, 8 cm tall, 600 g each) stand on their 5 x 12 cm faces on the rack's floor, long side left to right, their centres 36 cm left of centre and 20 and 30 cm in front of the arm bases (5 cm apart). A green plastic transfer pad, 8 cm front to back, 16 cm side to side and 1 cm thick, is fixed on the centre line, its centre 15 cm in front of the arm bases. Tape marks for scoring and reset: a thin tape cross on the table at each vial's start centre, its arms reaching 2 cm past the vial's base so they stay visible, and a tape cross on the blue block's top face at its centre (directly above the seat point). Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: Each vial's line runs, seen from above, from the vial's centre to the centre of the blue block. A brick counts as standing when its 8 cm axis is within 10 degrees of vertical (either 5 x 12 cm face down) and its centre is within 5 mm of 4 cm above the table (on the table itself: not on the pad, the rack or another brick; leaning onto a 12 cm edge lifts the centre past the 5 mm limit at about 4 degrees, so such a brick must be nearly vertical). A standing brick is across a vial's line when its footprint crosses the line and its centre is at most 4 cm from the line, measured square to it. For each vial: 0.5 if a standing brick is across its line and the brick's nearest edge is 5 mm to 12 cm from the vial's edge; 0.25 instead if that distance is more than 12 cm and at most 25 cm; otherwise 0. Each brick counts for one vial only (the pairing that scores most). A vial scores 0 if any brick, standing or fallen, has its outline seen from above closer than 5 mm to the vial and its bottom less than 2 mm above the vial's top. All of it, both vials shielded within 12 cm: 1.0. If either vial's centre has moved more than 1 cm from its start, it is tilted more than 10 degrees, or its bottom is more than 3 mm above the table (it has been lifted), the score is 0. How the second brick reaches the right vial (the pad handover) is not scored; only the end state is.
reset_notes: Stand both bricks back in the rack on their 5 x 12 cm faces, long side left to right, 20 and 30 cm in front of the arm bases. Check the vials are centred on their tape crosses on the table (25 cm in front, 15 cm left and right of centre); if a vial moved, put it back on its cross. The rack, pad and block are fixed and stay put; check the block's tape cross is still at its centre, 70 cm in front of the arm bases on the centre line.
fidelity: Approximate: the bricks are 600 g stand-ins (real lead bricks of this size weigh about 5 kg) and nothing is radioactive; the line to the seat is a 2D top-view line, not a dose model. The vials are solid cylinders. The rack, pad and seat block are fixed in place (clamp or tape them down for real trials). Every object has the same rubber-like friction (1.2 static, 1.0 dynamic), grippier than plastic or lead.
